tldr_label: TL;DR: Nvidia's board weighs ousting Jensen Huang, US envoys head to Putin, and Indonesia's vice president resigns

tldr_bullets.label: Nvidia
tldr_bullets.body: The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang after a second affair allegation. A late board meeting ended without an announced decision, and the shares fell sharply after hours. [[TAG:danger:CEO fate pending]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Witkoff and Kushner arrived in Moscow to meet Putin after the Abu Dhabi talks ended without a breakthrough. France says the EU will approve new Russia sanctions on Monday. [[TAG:info:shuttle diplomacy]]

tldr_bullets.label: Gaza
tldr_bullets.body: Gaza health authorities said an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital killed six people. Israel says it targeted a senior Hamas militant. [[TAG:danger:hospital strike]]

tldr_bullets.label: Indonesia
tldr_bullets.body: Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned after courts ruled that his education documents did not meet election requirements. [[TAG:warning:political shake-up]]

tldr_bullets.label: Washington
tldr_bullets.body: With a month until the December 11 funding deadline, the Washington Post reports Congress is far from a deal. [[TAG:warning:shutdown risk]]

sections.title: Nvidia: The Huang Question
sections.summary: Board meets on removing its founder-CEO after a second affair report; shares slide after hours

paragraphs.heading: Ouster Talk
paragraphs.body: ABC News and CBS News, citing The Wall Street Journal, reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang. According to The New York Times, as cited by ABC News, Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, a vice president who reports to him. Neither Nvidia, Powell nor Huang has confirmed it. The report follows an earlier allegation that US officials believe Huang had a relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. ABC News reported that Huang told staff he had been 'unfaithful' and apologized to his family. [[TAG:danger:second allegation]]

paragraphs.heading: No Decision Yet
paragraphs.body: CNBC and The Next Web reported that a board meeting on Huang's future ran into Wednesday night without an announced decision. CBS News said the bylaws let a majority of the 11 directors remove him as CEO with or without cause, and removal would not take him off the board. Yahoo Finance noted that Nvidia has no obvious successor. Days earlier, the board's own statement had expressed confidence in Huang. [[TAG:warning:watch for announcement]]

paragraphs.heading: Market Fallout
paragraphs.body: Nvidia closed up 2.87% on Wednesday as CoreWeave's results lifted AI stocks, according to Gotrade and the Motley Fool. CNBC reported that the S&P 500 rose 1.31% and the Nasdaq 1.60%. Nvidia then fell sharply after hours, with reported declines ranging from about 7% to more than 9%. AP reported that Asian shares mostly slipped on Thursday, with Taiwan's benchmark down 2.6% as Nvidia suppliers fell. Brent eased to about $92. [[TAG:danger:after-hours plunge]]

sections.title: Ukraine: From Abu Dhabi to Moscow
sections.summary: Witkoff and Kushner reach Moscow to meet Putin; EU readies sanctions on 150 entities, 50 banks

paragraphs.heading: Envoys to Putin
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and The Moscow Times reported that US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Thursday for talks with Putin. CNN said the trip follows Abu Dhabi talks that ended without a breakthrough. Yahoo News Singapore reported that Kushner said the envoys would seek Moscow's 'blessing' to bring European representatives into the negotiations. Hromadske said the envoys plan to meet Zelensky in Dublin next. [[TAG:info:Dublin next]]

paragraphs.heading: Why It Stalled
paragraphs.body: Forbes said the Abu Dhabi round produced no major breakthrough, and no date or venue for the next trilateral round has been set. Ukraine wants legally binding security guarantees and refuses to give up territory it controls. Russia demands all of Donbas and opposes Ukraine joining military alliances. According to Anadolu, Ukrainian negotiator Rustem Umerov listed a cessation of hostilities, security guarantees, economic recovery and humanitarian steps as priorities. [[TAG:danger:Donbas deadlock]]

paragraphs.heading: Sanctions
paragraphs.body: Reuters, carried by ThePrint and the Irish Examiner, reported that French Europe minister Benjamin Haddad said the EU will approve new Russia sanctions on Monday covering 150 more entities and 50 banks. France proposed most of the entities. Russia separately barred a Le Monde reporter and two French lawmakers from entry in a dispute over France's expulsion of Xenia Fedorova. [[TAG:warning:sanctions Monday]]

sections.title: Israel and Gaza
sections.summary: Eisenkot weighs Haredi and Arab-party options and warns against new war; Nasser Hospital hit

paragraphs.heading: Coalition Options
paragraphs.body: The Jerusalem Post and IBTimes reported that, with Likud talks off, Eisenkot's bloc is weighing a deal with the Haredi parties or a government relying on Arab-party support, amid internal divisions. The Times of Israel reported that Haredi leaders are considering a coalition deal while protesters rallied against the military draft. Ynet said Netanyahu renewed his call for a unity government. [[TAG:info:28-day clock]]

paragraphs.heading: No Return to War
paragraphs.body: The National and Jewish Insider reported that Eisenkot warned Netanyahu against launching a major military operation during coalition talks. He said Israel should not return to war unless it faces an immediate threat. Jewish Insider reported that the two will meet for a security briefing. [[TAG:warning:security dispute]]

paragraphs.heading: Nasser Hospital
paragraphs.body: CBS News, citing AP, and ABC News (Australia) reported that an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis early Thursday killed six people, including a surgeon, according to Gaza health authorities. Reported injury counts range from about a dozen to at least 28. Israel's military said it targeted a senior Hamas militant operating inside the hospital, and CBS noted it provided no evidence. Hamas called the strike a war crime. [[TAG:danger:six killed]]

sections.title: Washington
sections.summary: A month from the Dec 11 funding cliff, Congress is far from a deal; Rubio says no need for combat

paragraphs.heading: Funding Cliff
paragraphs.body: The Washington Post reported that Congress remains far from a deal to fund the government, a month before the December 11 deadline. A lapse would be the fourth shutdown of Trump's second term. Democrats want a short-term bill at current levels until next year. Republicans want to use their last weeks in control to fund the Iran war. Fox News described a crowded lame-duck session that also includes leadership races. [[TAG:warning:Dec 11 deadline]]

paragraphs.heading: Iran Posture
paragraphs.body: CBS News' live coverage reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking at the G7 in Paris, said there was 'no need' to restart major combat operations in Iran because economic pressure was working. The naval blockade of Iran's ports remains in place. [[TAG:info:pressure over strikes]]

sections.title: Indonesia's Vice President Quits
sections.summary: Gibran resigns after courts reject his education documents; parliament must pick a successor

paragraphs.heading: Resignation
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and the South China Morning Post reported that Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka resigned after the Constitutional Court and Supreme Court ruled last month that documents on his overseas education did not meet election requirements. Accounts differ on when he submitted the resignation: Al Jazeera says he offered it to President Prabowo on Tuesday, SCMP's Week Asia says Wednesday, and the assembly speaker says Thursday. He is the first vice president to resign mid-term since the democratic transition in 1998. [[TAG:warning:first since 1998]]

paragraphs.heading: What Comes Next
paragraphs.body: According to SCMP, the People's Consultative Assembly must choose a new vice president within 60 days from two candidates nominated by Prabowo. The outlet said the vacancy raises the stakes for the president's coalition alliances. [[TAG:info:60-day window]]

sections.title: Around the World
sections.summary: Record crowds greet Pope Leo in Peru; Guterres tells COP31 the climate crisis is 'outrunning us'

paragraphs.heading: Pope in Peru
paragraphs.body: CNN reported that Pope Leo XIV was welcomed by a record crowd in Peru, where he spent decades as a missionary and bishop. NCR reported that he told Peruvians he was 'returning to my homeland.' Reports said President Keiko Fujimori welcomed him at the Callao air base. America Magazine said the six-day visit includes Chiclayo, where he was bishop, on November 13, and Cuzco. [[TAG:success:homecoming]]

paragraphs.heading: COP31 Leaders
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that UN Secretary-General Guterres opened the COP31 leaders' summit by warning that 'the climate crisis is outrunning us.' UN News said he called the moment 'make or bake time' and urged a climate justice pact. Reuters, via ThePrint, reported that Turkish President Erdogan acknowledged three decades of talks have fallen short. The summit continues Thursday. [[TAG:warning:1.5C overshoot]]
